item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Town Council Meeting — 2026-10-15
item.description:
Mountain Village • 2026-10-15
A full plate for the October 15 Council meeting. Two housing authority items come first in consequence: second reading of an ordinance amending MVHA fee language in the Municipal Code (Sections 16.01 & 16.02) to point to an annual fee schedule rather than hardcoded figures, paired with a resolution adopting the actual 2027 MVHA fee schedules — including Village Court Apartments rents. The gondola project surfaces again with a fourth supplement to the intergovernmental cost-sharing agreement for the 2027 planning and development budget. A three-party MOU between Mountain Village, San Miguel County, and the Ridge at Telluride HOA on the Ridge View Plane interpretation heads to a vote — view plane disputes in this canyon have a long history. Council will also consider a town manager employment agreement for Michael Bouchard, a work session on expanding the Munchkins childcare program, a draft Beaver Management Plan, a food truck CUP renewal, and a sustainable tourism services agreement with the Telluride Tourism Board. The meeting closes with an executive session on sewer authority negotiations with the Town of Telluride.
⚡ Why it matters: Vote on MVHA fee ordinance and adoption of 2027 housing fee schedules.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Board of Trustees Public Hearing - Resolution No. 2026-0812 — 2026-10-15
item.description:
Town of Norwood • 2026-10-15
A single item is on the table in Norwood Thursday evening: Resolution No. 2026-0812, which sets the grounds and procedures for a potential removal-for-cause of a sitting Planning Commission member. The Board of Trustees will hear public testimony before deciding how to proceed. Removal of an appointed board member is uncommon — and when a small town moves to formalize that process, it usually means something significant has happened behind the scenes. The meeting is at Town Hall, 1670 Naturita Street, at 6:30 p.m., with a Zoom option available.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearing on formal removal of a sitting Planning Commission member.

item.title: [Thu, Oct 15] OPEN AUDITIONS: Elf The Musical
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Middle/High School, TELLURIDE Telluride Theatre wants YOU to audition for our Holiday Musical at the Sheridan Opera House. This year, we are performing ELF THE MUSICAL, based on the beloved film starring Will Ferrell. Actors of all ages and skill levels are encouraged to audition. Telluride Theatre is an educational theatre, from never-evers to seasoned professionals. This laugh-out-loud comedy performs on the Opera House stage December 17 – 23rd, plus an extra-special Christmas Eve matinee on the 24th. Don't know where to start? Don't worry, we’ll provide you what you need for the audition. Auditions will be held October 14 & 15 at Telluride Middle-High School, or you can submit a video audition if you’re out of town. To learn more and sign up for auditions, go to www.telluridetheatre.org/holiday.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Historic & Architectural Review Commission - Oct 21 2026 — 2026-10-21
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-21
The October 21 HARC meeting is anchored by the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project — the Town of Telluride's own large-scale development at 860 Black Bear Rd, zoned Accommodations 2. HARC takes up Buildings 1 and 2 as one public hearing item and Buildings 3 and 4 as a second, both continued from August 19. Each application covers new construction outside the Telluride Historic Landmark District exceeding 5,000 square feet of floor area under LUC 7-203.B.2.a.1. Also on the agenda: a payment-in-lieu of parking request for one space at 510 W Columbia Ave/129 N Townsend in the Historic Residential zone, where HARC is asked to support administrative approval. A small-scale new construction application at 785 Primrose Lane on a steep site is also up for review. The 448 Tomboy Road item has been continued to December 16 at the applicant's request, and the 214 S Fir Certificate of Appropriateness Amendment #2 — in the works since at least December 2025 — is being tabled for eight more months.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearings on four new buildings in the Town's own Shandoka redevelopment.
